angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 441,598 km at 134.31 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 7.4454 +/- 0.0137 mas (same row, RUWE 1.08): 134.31 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.634754 +/- 0.029302 solar radii from Dressing et al. 2017, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-90 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....154..207D/abstract): 441,598 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.704613 +/- 0.070461 solar masses from Dressing et al. 2017, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-90 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....154..207D/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4421.98 +/- 93.48 K from Dressing et al. 2017, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-90 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....154..207D/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Dressing et al. 2017, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-90 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....154..207D/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-90.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.681, rounded to two decimals

luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of K2-90 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.95318, from Barros et al. 2016 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016A&A...594A.100B/abstract)
